key_insight: Approximate unitary designs do match moments, but their output-probability distributions can still deviate from Haar randomness by a quantifiable amount unless extra structural invariance is present.
engineering_relevance: For quantum hardware and randomized circuit benchmarking, this gives a sharper guarantee of how well random circuits emulate ideal randomness and what additional circuit structure is needed to improve accuracy.
method: Proves Kolmogorov-distance bounds between single-output probabilities of strong \u03b5-approximate unitary k-designs and the finite-dimensional Porter-Thomas distribution.
Shows the bound is optimal up to constants for general strong approximate designs.
Uses local translation invariance on \log k+O(1) qubits to obtain exponentially better error decay and total-variation guarantees.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical error bounds scaling as O(\sqrt{2^n/(k(k+2^n))}+\u03b5) in general and 2^{-\u03a9(k)}+O(\u03b5) with local invariance, plus an entropy deviation bound of O(\sqrt{\eta}).
watch_item: The strongest guarantees require additional local invariance; moment matching alone does not ensure uniformly small distributional error for individual output probabilities.
paper_title: Random Quantum Circuits Beyond Moment Matching
